# Constructions

## In short
- Constructions are built with AP and with resources from the bank. The resources are only removed when the last AP is put in [1].
- Upgrading the Workshop (`small_refine_#00`) through daily votes lowers every construction's AP cost by up to 35% and raises the HP you repair per AP from 2 to 4 [2].
- Temporary constructions fall down after every attack and must be built again [3].
- In Pandemonium, construction sites start in hard mode (much bigger resource costs). Reading a blueprint makes an existing site cheaper instead of unlocking a new one, and the attack damages constructions every night [4].

## How it works

**Unlocking construction sites**
- When a town is created, it gets the base constructions available from the start. Then it gets the constructions listed in the `unlocked_buildings` and initially-constructed settings, unless they are disabled [5].
- A construction can only be added if its parent construction is already in the town [6].
- Adding a construction also adds, recursively, all its children whose effective rarity is 0 (no blueprint needed), unless they are disabled [6].
- A new site starts at difficulty level `OptModifierBuildingDifficulty` if its prototype supports hard mode, and at 0 otherwise [6].

**Blueprints and rarity**
- Blueprint level (rarity) ranges from 0 to 5 [7]:
  - 0: no blueprint needed (for example Wood Plating, Spikes).
  - 1 to 4: for example Water Catcher (1), Bonfire (2), Water Turrets (3), Reactor (4) [8].
  - 5: only the Chocolate Cross.
- The effective rarity of a construction is taken from the town setting `overrides.building_rarity`, checked in this order [9]:
  1. an entry with the construction's name;
  2. an entry `"<default rarity>>"`;
  3. a `*` wildcard;
  4. otherwise, the construction's own blueprint level.
- You must be in town to read a blueprint, and reading it uses it up [10].
  - Common plan (`bplan_c_#00`): unlocks rarity 1.
  - Rare plan (`bplan_r_#00`): unlocks rarity 3 [11].
  - Ruin plans use named lists instead. For example, the uncommon hotel plan uses `hotel_lv2`. Its card says it makes up 12% of finds in the Abandoned Hotel [12].
- What happens when you read a plan depends on the town's blueprint mode [13]:
  - **`unlock` mode (default):** the possible results are the not-yet-unlocked constructions whose rarity, named list or explicit list matches the plan. Disabled constructions are excluded. One is picked at random with equal chances and added as a new site.
  - **`improve` mode:** the possible results are sites that are not finished, have difficulty level ≤ 1, support hard mode, and are not in `fixed_building_rsc_level`. The same plan filter applies. Constructions whose parents are still at a level below 0 are left out, unless that would leave nothing. One site is picked at random, and its level becomes `max(1, level+1)`. So one plan takes a site from −1 (hard) to 1 (easy), and a second plan takes it to 2.
- Constructions that make plans every night:
  - Upgraded `small_refine_#01` at level 1: 4 common plans.
  - Level 2: 2 common and 2 uncommon, plus a 50% chance of 1 rare.
  - Level 3: 2 uncommon and 2 rare, plus a 50% chance of 1 very rare [14].
  - Separately, `small_refine_#01` makes 1 common plan every day. `small_strategy_#01` makes plans by level, from 1 uncommon at level 0 up to 1 rare plus a 10% chance of 1 very rare at level 4 [15].

**Cost (AP and resources)**
- Each construction has resource sets of three types:
  - Hard, used when the difficulty level is below 0;
  - Easy, used when it is above 0;
  - Default, used at 0.
- The set also depends on how many times the construction has already been completed (for constructions that can be built again) [16].
- If no set of the needed type exists, the game uses the Default set [17].
- Example, Water Turrets [8]:

| Mode | Metal Support | Copper Pipe | Water Ration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default | 10 | 6 | 25 |
| Hard | 30 | 24 | 75 |
| Easy | 6 | 5 | 19 |

  The AP is 50 in all three modes.
- **Base AP:**
  - If the difficulty level is 2 or more: base AP = `floor(setAP × f^(level−1))`.
  - Otherwise the base AP is not changed [16].
  - `f` depends on rarity: 0.65 for rarity 0 or 1, 0.70 for 2, 0.75 for 3, 0.85 for 4, and 1 for anything else [16].
- **AP still needed to finish a site:** `ceil((round(baseAP × ConstructionAPRatio) − AP already invested) × S)`. S is 2/3 for a banished citizen working with the slavery bonus, and 1 otherwise [1].
- Rules when you invest AP [1]:
  - You cannot invest more than is missing. Investing 0 is refused while AP is still missing.
  - The action is refused if you have a hand injury (`wound3`), if a parent construction is not finished, if you are tired, or if you lack enough points.
  - All the resources must be in the bank.
  - Points: **construction points (CP) are used first, then AP.** The code gives CP as the main point type and AP as the fallback.
- When the last AP goes in [1]:
  - the site is complete;
  - the resources are taken from the bank;
  - a log entry is written and the construction's effects are triggered;
  - all recommendation votes for it are cleared.
- Investment logs are only written if the Building Registry (`item_rp_book2_#00`) is built [1].

**Repairs**
- AP needed: `ceil((maxHP − HP) / RepairAPRatio)`.
- Each AP restores `RepairAPRatio` HP, up to the maximum.
- Defense becomes `floor(min(base def, base def × HP / maxHP))` [1].
- Banished citizens can always repair, even without the Ministry of Slavery [1].

**Damage and destruction**
- When a construction is destroyed, it becomes unfinished and its AP, defense, HP and level go back to 0. Its child constructions are not affected [6].
- Damage the constructions do to themselves:
  - The Reactor (`small_arma_#00`) takes 50–125 damage each night, before the daily upgrade.
  - The Fireworks (`small_fireworks_#00`) take 20 damage each night [18].
  - If the Fireworks are destroyed during the attack, the town gets +300 temporary defense [19].
- **Attack damage** (only when `OptModifierBuildingDamage` is on) [3]:
  - Total damage = `round((zombies − zombies stopped by the watch) × 0.2)`.
  - Possible targets are constructions that are finished, have max HP above 0, are not temporary, and are not impervious. They are hit in random order.
  - Each target takes `min(remaining damage, HP, rand(ceil(10% maxHP), maxHP))`, then capped at `ceil(70% maxHP)`.
  - The damage before the 70% cap is what gets subtracted from the total, so the part above the cap is lost.
  - Defense becomes `round(base def × HP / maxHP)`. A construction at 0 HP is destroyed.

**Temporary constructions**
- After the attack, every finished temporary construction becomes unfinished, with 0 AP and no construction date [3].
- All temporary defense bonuses, for each construction and for the town, are then reset to 0 [3].
- Examples: Wood Plating (40 def, 20 AP), Guerilla Traps (60 def, 30 AP), Holy Raincloud (200 def, 40 AP), Mines (115 def, 50 AP) [20].

## What changes it

**Workshop level** [2]

| Workshop level | 0 (or not built) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ConstructionAPRatio | 1.0 | 0.94 | 0.88 | 0.82 | 0.75 | 0.65 |
| RepairAPRatio (HP per AP) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 4 |

The Workshop card describes the same values [21].

**Other modifiers**
- **Technician (`tech`):** has 6 construction points; every other job has 0 [22].
- **Ministry of Slavery (`small_slave_#00`):** lets banished citizens build. Each of their AP counts as `floor(AP × 1.5)`, and the missing-AP amount is multiplied by 2/3 [1].
- **Hand injury (`wound3`):** you cannot build or repair at all [1].
- **Settings:**
  - `modifiers.building_difficulty`: the starting difficulty level. Default 0 [23].
  - `features.blueprint_mode`: default `unlock` [24].
  - `modifiers.building_attack_damage`: default off [23].
  - `fixed_building_rsc_level`: default empty [25].
  - `overrides.building_rarity` and disabled buildings [9].

## Town types
- **Default:** difficulty 0, `unlock` mode, no attack damage [23].
- **Small:** also starts with the Searchtower (`small_gather_#02`) unlocked [26].
- **Remote:** no construction differences; only the soul generation factor changes [27].
- **Panda (Pandemonium)** [4]:
  - Difficulty −1 (Hard resource sets).
  - `improve` blueprint mode.
  - Attack damage to constructions is on.
  - Defense items in the bank are destroyed: up to 20 per night, ratio 50.
  - Rarity overrides: `"0>": 5` gives constructions that normally need no blueprint rarity 5, so they no longer unlock on their own. To compensate, a long `unlocked_buildings` list unlocks almost the whole tree at the start.
  - Several constructions get set rarities, for example Wood Plating 1 and Fireworks 2.
  - The ruin blueprint lists are also different.
- **Custom:** every setting above can be changed. When the rules are cleaned up, unknown disabled or unlocked constructions are removed, and unlocked ones must be unlockable by a blueprint [28].
